questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Reversal caused by dividing by a negative
questions.learningObjective: solve a rule for a variable and round to a whole number
questions.stem: A table of signal readings reads 1 | 4 units, 2 | 9 units, 3 | 15 units. A model says 5r - 14 >= 3s. At s = 4, what is the least whole number r that satisfies the model?
questions.explanation: Substituting s = 4 gives 5r - 14 >= 12, so 5r >= 26 and r >= 5.2. The least whole number that satisfies the model is 6, since 5 falls short of 5.2 and fails the rule.
questions.hint: Substitute s = 4, then divide by 5.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Negating an inequality statement
questions.learningObjective: correct a rule that was moved to the wrong side
questions.stem: A table of stops and minutes reads Courier A | 14 stops, Courier B | 21 stops, Courier C | 33 stops. A rule is 3d + 20 <= 4k - 10. A student solves this as 3d <= 4k + 10 and then reports that every stop qualifies. What is the flaw?

options.text: Subtracting 20 gives 3d <= 4k - 30, so the student bound is too generous
Adding the two sides gives 3d + 4k >= -10, the correct combined form
options.misconception: adds the sides instead of subtracting one term

options.text: The rule can only be solved for k, so no bound on d exists at all
options.misconception: claims the variable cannot be isolated

options.text: A rule with a plus sign describes a half-plane, so every point qualifies
options.misconception: believes a half-plane contains all points

questions.explanation: Subtracting 20 from both sides of 3d + 20 <= 4k - 10 gives 3d <= 4k - 30, not 4k + 10. The student bound keeps extra points, so the claim that every stop qualifies does not follow.
questions.hint: Move the 20 to the right side before dividing.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: A system of inequalities as simultaneous conditions
questions.learningObjective: explain what it means for a point to satisfy a system
questions.stem: A table of freight and weight reads 3 cartons | 45 pounds, 5 cartons | 70 pounds, 8 cartons | 110 pounds. A freight rule is 4s - 3w <= 0 and 2s + w <= 60. Explain what it means for a shipment point to satisfy this system, and why one rule alone is not enough.

answer.exemplar: Satisfying the system means the proposed point meets both conditions at once, so 4s - 3w must be at most 0 and 2s + w must be at most 60. Passing only the first rule would allow points whose second expression is far too large, such as a heavy carton with many shipments, and passing only the second would allow points outside the shaded side. The system keeps exactly the overlap of the two half-planes.

questions.explanation: A point must meet both conditions at the same time, so 4s - 3w has to be at most 0 and 2s + w at most 60. Checking only one condition would keep points the system rejects.
questions.hint: A system asks for every condition at once.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Intersection of two half-planes
questions.learningObjective: find the greatest table value inside an overlap of two rules
questions.stem: A table of jobs and discounts reads Job 1 | 18 dollars, Job 2 | 26 dollars, Job 3 | 41 dollars. Two rules apply: 3o - 24 >= 0 and o - 20 <= 10. What is the greatest value in the table that satisfies both rules at the same time?
questions.explanation: The first rule needs 3o at least 24, so o at least 8, which every row clears. The second rule needs o at most 30, and 41 is past that, so 26 is the greatest value that fits both.
questions.hint: Turn each rule into a range for o.

questions.topic: Corner where two boundary lines cross
questions.learningObjective: solve a pair of boundary lines for a corner coordinate
questions.stem: A table of blocks and output reads Block 1 | 30 units, Block 2 | 44 units, Block 3 | 58 units. The boundary lines are 2x + y = 50 and x - 2y = 10. First find the corner where the lines cross, then state the value of x at that corner.

options.text: The corner is (22, 6), so the value of x at the corner is 22
The corner is (6, 22), so the value of x at the corner is 6
options.misconception: swaps the two coordinates of the corner

options.text: The corner is (50, 0), so the value of x at the corner is 50
options.misconception: takes an intercept of the first line as the corner

options.text: The corner is (12, 26), so the value of x at the corner is 12
options.misconception: adds the two line equations and reads the sum as a coordinate

questions.explanation: From 2x + y = 50, y = 50 - 2x, and substituting into x - 2y = 10 gives x - 2(50 - 2x) = 10, so 5x = 110 and x = 22. Then y = 50 - 44 = 6, so the corner is (22, 6).
questions.hint: Solve the first line for y, then substitute.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Feasibility of a candidate point
questions.learningObjective: state where a feasible point must sit for two rules
questions.stem: A table of readings and limits reads Reading 1 | 15, Reading 2 | 20, Reading 3 | 25. A lab rule is 2x - y <= 15 and x + y >= 5. Which statement about a proposed point is correct?

options.text: The point is feasible when it lies above both boundary lines
The point is feasible when it lies below both boundary lines
options.misconception: misreads the direction of the inequality for y

options.text: The point is feasible when it lies between the two boundary lines
options.misconception: picks the strip between the lines instead of the overlap

options.text: The point is feasible when it lies on either of the two boundary lines
options.misconception: confuses boundary points with the whole region

questions.explanation: The rule 2x - y <= 15 means y >= 2x - 15, and x + y >= 5 means y >= 5 - x. A point must be above both lines, so the feasible region is the overlap of the two half-planes.
questions.hint: Rewrite each rule so that it bounds y from below.
